meta.label: 1차 티어·포지션 순위 공개 · 검수 중
meta.source: ChatGPT and user discussion; requires further historical validation
meta.note: PUBLIC PRELIMINARY TIER DRAFT: 148 players have provisional S–D tiers and position-specific ranks, which are not overall rankings. Best XI uses a historically representative 4-2-3-1 with Djalminha as CAM and Raúl as the sole ST. Formation statistical dominance across all 1999-00 league matches has not been independently verified; only 21/148 three-season audits complete.

excludedProvisionalCandidates.name: Eduardo Estíbariz
excludedProvisionalCandidates.reason: Historical RB listed behind Jesús Cota and Jordi Ferrón; only two RB candidates allowed; 1999–00 role requires further review.

tierProposal.scope: 148 provisional S-D tiers published; per-position 1..N ranks now assigned across all 148 players at user request; overall ranks are not displayed and Best XI approval remains pending
tierProposal.sourceNotes: 1999-00 BDFutbol team lineups; FBref season statistics; 1999 and 2000 Ballon d'Or; UEFA 1999-00 club awards; initial historical contextual assessment
pendingCorrections: Helguera's actual 1999-00 CB vs DM minutes cannot be conclusively established from currently accessible period lineup data; CB 3-player cap requires a choice among Hierro/Karanka/Júlio César/Iván Campo
Revivo listed attacking midfield yet Celta 4-2-3-1 CAM-exclusion rule needs clarification before changing CAM eligibility
Cembranos CM retained provisionally; match-by-match positional role totals not yet verified
Historical 1997-98 and 1998-99 individual records corroborated for 21 of 148 candidates; remaining 127 need evidence
Team-level shortlist omissions such as Ronald de Boer, Jari Litmanen and Iván Campo require reassessment under 2-per-position and CB 3-per-team constraints

positionAudit.Helguera: proposed CB, season-level CB-vs-DM starting count still unresolved
positionAudit.Cembranos: CM retained, evidence does not establish CAM majority
positionAudit.Revivo: proposed CAM, 4-2-3-1 two-midfield CAM-exclusion rule unresolved
positionAudit.Rayo and Madrid GK: Lopetegui and Bizzarri both retained as starter-equivalent backups (10 and 11 combined league/UCL starts respectively)

bestXiReview.label: 1999–00 베스트 XI 1차 선정안 · 검수 전
bestXiReview.notes: Eleven-player 4-2-3-1 provisional XI with a true attacking midfielder (Djalminha) behind Raúl. The former 4-4-2 XI's second striker Roy Makaay is omitted from the eleven, not removed from the candidate list. Positions and historical formation-frequency evidence require continued review.
bestXiReview.selectionLogic: Historically representative 1999-00 Spanish 4-2-3-1: GK1, RB1, CB2, LB1, DM1, CM1, CAM1, LW1, RW1, ST1. Each pick is #1 or within the top two for CB; positional ranks across all 148 unchanged.

meta.crestSources: Club images sourced from football-data.org and football-logos.cc. Deportivo's prior assumed /spain/512 URL was replaced with an image-indexed published asset URL; displayed image is a later Deportivo crest (2000–2026 style), not the historic 1997–2000 matchday emblem.

positionalRanking.label: 포지션별 순위 배정 완료
positionalRanking.scope: All 148 existing 1999-00 La Liga candidates; ranks run from 1 to number of candidates within each individual primary position, no cross-position overall rank
positionalRanking.process: Current previously published provisional S–D tiers first; position-specific historically informed manual priority within a tier; league starts and named starting role as tie-breakers; alphabetical stable final tie-break
positionalRanking.note: Rank order is assigned for website presentation by direct user request. Existing preliminary player-tier data and three-season evidence review remain provisional; this is not a verified final historical ranking.

formationEvidence.summary: 4-2-3-1 selected as a historically representative and increasingly widespread Spanish top-flight system around 1999-2000, not as a statistically verified #1 across all 380 league games.
formationEvidence.examples: El País 1999-11-30 identifies Deportivo and Celta using 4-2-3-1 in the season; Diario AS 2001-07-31 describes the system's spread at Deportivo, Celta, Zaragoza and Real Madrid.
formationEvidence.caveat: Formation selection should be revised if a comprehensive season-wide count identifies a different most common shape.

crestHistoricalReview.note: The 1999–00 crest was the brighter 1997–2000 variant, not the later gold-and-purple 2000–2026 version. A viewable later-version image has been installed to replace a guessed URL; when a directly embeddable reliable 1997–2000 asset is sourced, replace this display URL.

qualifiers.route: 2000 Intertoto; also qualified for 2000–01 UEFA Cup via Intertoto
